title: Ample invertible module on a quasi-compact open in a locally finite type group
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and $H/k$ a separated group scheme locally of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $U\subseteq H$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], then $U$ is a finite-type $k$-scheme and admits an absolutely ample invertible $\mathcal O_U$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. The open $U$ need not be a subgroup or a union of connected components; $H$ need not be quasi-compact, smooth, reduced, connected or commutative, and $k$ need not be perfect.

source.place: Tags 0B7R (proposition-connected-component) and 0BF7 (lemma-algebraic-quasi-projective), adapted from finite-type groups to quasi-compact opens of locally finite type groups; varieties.tex Tag 0BDC (lemma-ample-after-field-extension). Over an algebraic closure a quasi-compact open meets finitely many clopen translates of the finite-type neutral group; restrict the ample modules on those translates and descend existence of an ample module. This extension to opens is the auxiliary assertion, not the finite-type-group assertion itself.

proof.text: For $u\in U$, choose an affine finite-type chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq H$ containing $u$. Principal opens are a basis, so choose $D(f)$ containing $u$ inside $U\cap\operatorname{Spec}A$. The ring $A_f$ is generated over $k$ by generators of $A$ and $f^{-1}$. Thus $U$ is locally of finite type. Quasi-compactness selects finitely many such charts, proving that $U/k$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This argument also applies when $U$ is empty, with the empty cover.

Choose an algebraic closure $K/k$ and form $H_K$ and $U_K$ using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Multiplication, inverse and unit of $H$ base change to $H_K$; their group diagrams still commute, since equality can be checked on both projections in the fibre-product universal property. Thus $H_K$ is a group scheme. It is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], $U_K$ is open in $H_K$, and by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] applied to the finite-type scheme $U/k$ of step 1, $U_K/K$ is finite type, hence quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0BF7, lemma-algebraic-quasi-projective, first reduction; Morphisms Tag 01T4, lemma-base-change-finite-type.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-lft-field-group-neutral-component], $C=(H_K)^0$ is a clopen finite-type subgroup with its original open-subscheme structure. Every connected component $D$ of $H_K$ contains a $K$-point: for $x\in D$, the nonempty closure $Z=\overline{\{x\}}$ is connected and lies in $D$ by maximality of the component. The Jacobson statement [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] gives a point $z\in Z$ closed in $H_K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], its residue field is $K$ over $K$, giving $g\in H_K(K)$ in $D$. The translation $L_g$ is an isomorphism with inverse $L_{g^{-1}}$ by [lem-sc-translation-automorphism]; its defining formula gives $L_g(e)=g$. A homeomorphism carries a maximal connected subset to a maximal connected subset, so $L_g(C)=D$. Restricting the inverse scheme isomorphisms to these opens gives $C\simeq D$. Hence all components are clopen finite-type schemes. They partition $H_K$: the union of connected subsets through a point is connected and maximal, and two such maximal sets that intersect coincide. Quasi-compactness of $U_K$ now gives finitely many components $D_1,\ldots,D_r$ covering $U_K$.

source.place: Tags 0B7R, proposition-connected-component, and 0BF7, lemma-algebraic-quasi-projective, component reduction; Varieties Tag 0478 and Morphisms Tag 01TB.

proof.text: The finite-type group $C/K$ is separated by [lem-sc-group-scheme-separated-field]. Thus [lem-sfb-finite-type-group-ample-line] supplies an ample invertible module $A$ on $C$. Put $U_j=U_K\cap D_j$. It is closed in the quasi-compact space $U_K$ because $D_j$ is clopen, hence is quasi-compact. Under $D_j\simeq C$, the inclusion $U_j\subseteq D_j$ becomes an open immersion $a_j:U_j\to C$. Apply [lem-sfb-ample-pullback-qc-immersion] to obtain the ample invertible module $B_j=a_j^*A$ on $U_j$. This is precisely where one must allow $U$ to cut a component in a proper open subset.

The $U_j$ form a finite disjoint clopen cover of $U_K$. Define $B(V)=\prod_{j=1}^r B_j(V\cap U_j)$ with componentwise module operations and restriction maps. The sheaf axiom holds factor by factor, and locally on $U_j$ this is $B_j$, so $B$ is invertible. For $x\in U_j$, ampleness of $B_j$ gives $n\geq1$ and a section $s_j$ of $B_j^{\otimes n}$ with affine nonvanishing locus containing $x$. The componentwise description of tensor powers lets us extend $s_j$ by zero to a section of $B^{\otimes n}$ on $U_K$. Its nonvanishing locus is exactly the same affine open of $U_j$. Since $U_K$ is quasi-compact, these witnesses verify [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], so $B$ is ample. For $r=0$, $U_K$ is empty and the unique module is locally invertible and ample by the same definition.

source.place: Tag 01PS, definition-ample, finite disjoint clopen gluing and zero extension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ample-existence-field-extension] to the $k$-scheme $U$, the field extension $K/k$, and the ample invertible module $B$ on $U_K$. It supplies an absolutely ample invertible module on $U$; this descends existence and does not assert descent of the specified module $B$. Step 1 already proved the finite-type assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q26-c66980897 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, the new node lem-sfb-ample-pullback-qc-immersion, and the statement of every cited node. Sources checked against the Stacks tex: 0B3E(2) at properties.tex:4759 (X' quasi-compact and i an immersion ⇒ i^*L ample) is stated exactly by the new node. 0BDC at varieties.tex:2740 matches lem-sfb-ample-existence-field-extension. 0BF7 at groupoids.tex:1365 and 0B7R at 1013: the proof follows their reduction, extended from finite-type groups to quasi-compact opens; proof_origin is correctly agent. Step 1: localizing a finite-type chart at a principal open plus quasi-compactness gives finite type, including U empty. Step 2: lft and open-immersion base change are mathlib leaves, and finite-type base change is applied to U, not to H. Step 3: the neutral-component lemma covers any field and non-quasi-compact lft groups. Every connected component contains a closed point by the Jacobson lemma, that point is K-rational by the residue-field lemma, and translation by it maps C onto the component; the quasi-compact U_K meets only finitely many components. Step 4: C is separated and of finite type, so the finite-type-group ample lemma applies. Each U_j is clopen in U_K, hence quasi-compact, so 0B3E(2) restricts the ample module to U_j; this is needed when U is a proper open of a component. Step 5: gluing on a finite disjoint clopen cover with zero-extended witnesses is elementary; the existing lem-trf-finite-coproduct-ample-with-points would also serve but citing it is optional. Step 6: 0BDC. The new node is not a duplicate: lem-trf-ample-restrict-closed-immersion covers closed immersions only, lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible covers affine morphisms only, and lem-trf-proj-qc-open-twist-ample is about twisting sheaves on Proj; rg finds no other 0B3E node, and Mathlib has no notion of ampleness. Edge cases tested: empty U, alpha_p, an infinite constant group, an elliptic curve E times an infinite constant group with U a proper open of one component, identity and empty immersions. The off-unit citations declared in tool_uses are generic and accepted.
